chapters.title: Wren Hollow
chapters.text: The village council gives you the stewardship of the hollow: a patch of standing forest cut into plots, and a ledger with more questions than answers. Everyone agrees the trees are worth something. Nobody agrees on what, or how quickly.

chapters.title: The first cut
chapters.text: The first plot comes down and the money arrives the same afternoon. It pays the bills and quiets the doubters, and it leaves a bare patch of ground you will pass every morning.

chapters.title: Something in the ground
chapters.text: You put saplings into the bare plot, more out of stubbornness than strategy. Nothing looks different yet, but the soil is no longer just waiting.

chapters.title: A thousand in the ledger
chapters.text: The harvest income crosses a thousand, and the village hall gets its new roof. It is hard to argue with a roof, and you notice that nobody asks how the forest is doing.

chapters.title: The habit forms
chapters.text: By the fifteenth cut, clearing has stopped feeling like a decision and started feeling like a routine. The saw is quick, the numbers are steady, and the horizon of the forest has quietly moved back.

chapters.title: Ground that remembers
chapters.text: You have cleared the same plot five times, and each time it gave a little less. The soil keeps a record of everything asked of it, even when the ledger does not.

chapters.title: Yes, of course
chapters.text: Ten times now, a neighbour has asked for something from the hollow and ten times you have said yes. It has made you well liked, and it has made the forest a little smaller for each favour.

chapters.title: Ten noes
chapters.text: You have turned down ten requests, each with the same steady explanation. Some neighbours grumble at the gate, but a few start to say that they at least know where you stand.

chapters.title: Talking again
chapters.text: There was a season when hardly anyone in the village would meet your eye. Slowly, through small kept promises, the greetings return, and the council asks for your opinion again.

chapters.title: One tree that stayed
chapters.text: One plot has grown all the way to maturity without a saw near it. Standing under it, you can tell the difference between a forest that is being used and a forest that is simply allowed to be.

chapters.title: The bare plot is green
chapters.text: The plot you replanted is fully back. It took longer than the cutting did, and it is a little different from what stood there before, but it is unmistakably a forest again.

chapters.title: Something in the branches
chapters.text: You catch movement in the canopy, and then the unmistakable sound of a wren. Wherever the trees have had time to settle, other things have started to move in.

chapters.title: Not a single stump
chapters.text: The hollow is worth three hundred and you have not cleared a single plot to get there. It is a slower kind of pride than a full ledger, but a steadier one.

chapters.title: A busier forest
chapters.text: Across the hollow, the small signs of life add up: droppings on the paths, nests in old forks, tracks in the mud after rain. The forest has stopped being scenery and started being a neighbourhood.

chapters.title: A forest worth a thousand
chapters.text: The trees themselves are now worth a thousand, without a single one of them being sold. The value was there all along, and it grew every season you left it alone.

chapters.title: The whole village behind you
chapters.text: Relations with the village reach their peak. People stop you on the road to ask how the hollow is doing, and this time they clearly mean it.

chapters.title: Ten plots alive
chapters.text: Wildlife now moves through ten plots at once. Tracks cross where you used to draw plot boundaries, and the animals ignore the grid entirely.

chapters.title: Both columns full
chapters.text: There are five hundred in the income column and five hundred in the standing forest. The old argument between spending and keeping turns out to have a middle path, if you are patient with it.

chapters.title: Five old giants
chapters.text: Five plots stand at full maturity together, the tallest thing for miles. Their crowns have started to touch, and the light on the forest floor turns green and slow.

chapters.title: The whole life cycle
chapters.text: Walking the hollow, you can point out a bare plot, a seedling patch, a preserved stand and a fully recovered one all within sight of each other. It is a forest in every stage of its life, and every stage has a reason.

chapters.title: The Highland Grove
chapters.text: The council opens the Highland Grove above the hollow, a second stretch of forest that is now yours to look after. It is a chance to apply everything you learned the slow way.

chapters.title: The canopy closes
chapters.text: Every plot is either standing or well on its way back, with nothing bare left to mend. Looking up from the path, you cannot find a gap in the leaves, and for the first time you are not looking for one.

chapters.title: A grove, not a patch
chapters.text: Somewhere in the last few seasons the plots stopped being separate. Walking the path now, you pass from shade to shade without noticing the joins, and the children have started calling it the grove. You let them.

chapters.title: Woodland
chapters.text: The council clerk asks what to write on the map, because "the plots" no longer covers it. You suggest a word older than the ledger. She writes it in ink, and it looks right there, as if it had always been waiting.

chapters.title: What the old trees keep
chapters.text: On a still evening you stand under trunks that were saplings when you took the ledger, and will be here long after your handwriting fades. You are not the owner of this place, you realise. You are the one who was trusted to stay.
